title: A woman and child among the sandbags, Núi Bà Đen
description: A Vietnamese woman in a pale blouse and long dark skirt stands with a small child in red in a gap between deep sandbag walls. Behind her, a shelter of lashed poles, canvas and matting holds ammunition cans, a square tin, pots, a helmet liner and crates; boulders rise at right with an empty table frame on top, and the cloud layer lies below. Larry's comment is about the mountain rather than the people in the frame: "It takes 27 hours to walk up the mountain."
researchNotes: Larry's comment of 2026-09-12 (giscus-vn-0037-c18416114.json) gives the place and the climb; he did not speak about the woman or the child, who are unnamed. The 27 hours is his figure and is not checked. The shelter is of the scrap-built kind he described for the summit's residents at VN-0039 — 'to get a stick like that you would go down into the jungle and carry it up.'
